# orkumo CLI

Talks to the local Orkumo API (`{{API_URL}}`). Invocation: `orkumo <command>`; if the shell does
not find it, `"$ORKUMO_CLI" <command>` or `"{{CLI}}" <command>`. Exit code 0 on success, 1 on an
API error, 2 on wrong usage; errors go to stderr and say how to recover.

## agents

```
orkumo agents [--all] [--json]
```

One block per agent: `id`, state (`working`, `needs input`, `done`, …), harness, project@branch,
name, then what it waits for, its PR links and the start of its last answer. Orchestrators are
marked `[orchestrator]`. Without `--all` finished agents older than a day and terminals Orkumo does
not run are left out. `--json` prints the raw overview (`GET /api/orchestrator/overview`).

## show

```
orkumo show <id> [--last N]
```

The last N (default 10, max 100) user/assistant turns of the agent's transcript. Use it to verify
claims ("tests pass", "PR opened") before reporting them.

## send

```
orkumo send <id> <message…>
orkumo send <id> -          # message from stdin (long or multi-line)
```

Background Claude Code jobs get the message as a reply; agents running in an Orkumo pane get it
typed into their terminal and submitted. Agents running outside Orkumo cannot be reached: start a
new one instead.

## start

```
orkumo start --project <path|name> [--harness claude|omp] [--name <name>] <prompt…>
```

`--project`: an absolute path, or a project name from `orkumo projects` (case-insensitive, a unique
prefix is enough). Default harness: Orkumo's default. Claude Code starts as a background session
(`claude --bg`, `--name` names it); Oh My Pi starts in an Orkumo pane in the project and shows up in
the rail (it names its session itself). The prompt is the agent's whole briefing: goal, context,
acceptance criteria, what to report.

## stop

```
orkumo stop <id>
```

Stops a background job, an Oh My Pi session or the agent of an Orkumo pane.

## projects

```
orkumo projects [--json]
```

Name, path and number of listed agents of every project Orkumo scans.

## Ids

`<id>` is the id from `orkumo agents` (`a1b2c3`, `interactive-1234`, `omp-<uuid>`); a session
uuid, a pane id or a unique id prefix also works.
